newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumps in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index jumps in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index leaped 231 points, or 1.56 percent, to 15,122 in early Wednesday morning trade, boosted chiefly by Wall Street's overnight recovery and futures-related trading, brokers said.
The blue-chip index then rose to 15,200 before falling back to 15,155, up 264 points or 1.78 percent. Turnover was a huge HK$3.94 billion in the first 30 minutes of trade.
"It's due to the Dow," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities. "We could move to 15,500 ahead of the weekend."
The Dow Industrials rebounded overnight by 153.80 points, or 2.02 percent, to 7,758.06, recovering from a 192-point drop the previous day, its largest decline of the year.
Trade in Hang Seng Index futures led the cash market, brokers said.
The June contract, which expires on Thursday, moved to a high of 15,270 in early trade then eased to 15,195. The July contract leaped to 15,370 before falling back to 15,300.
"Sentiment is quite good before July 1," said Allen Pao, in institutional sales at South China Securities. "Both blue chips and red chips are sought after.
Market sentiment was lifted by the positive implications of China's recovery of Hong Kong on July 1, brokers said.
The Hong Kong market will be closed from June 28 through July 2 to mark the handover and will resume normal trading on July 3.
Property stocks led the market's rally, followed at a distance by finance issues.
Blue chip favourite Sun Hung Kai Properties led the sector, leaping HK$2.50 to HK$95.00 in early trade before easing to HK$94.00. New World Development added HK$1.10 to HK$47.80.
International banking giant HSBC Holdings jumped HK$7.00 to HK$235, just shy of its all time high of HK$236.
Red chip bank China Everbright-IHD was the most active, gaining HK$1.10 to HK$19.90 on trade of HK$308 million.
